summary: Upgrade R19 OpenXR swapchain teardown from submission-only Flush to a D3D11 event-query completion fence so normal-path GPU work is actually complete before xrDestroySwapchain.

C0_RECOVER.evidence: Recovered bookkeeping HEAD 6d33850a66a396d37c2f5cec53ab037ace59464c. Structural extraction remains terminal. CONVERSION-DX9EX-00453 exact material SHA 75066b77b9f95ca644791d4c821a1c77fffcfe1f passed DX9Ex Active 37405053984 and Domain Isolation 37405053923.

C1_REVIEW.evidence: OpenXR 1.1 requires submitted graphics commands referring to a swapchain to have completed execution before xrDestroySwapchain. Microsoft documents that ID3D11DeviceContext::Flush is asynchronous and recommends D3D11_QUERY_EVENT + GetData to determine GPU completion. 00453 therefore closed submission ordering but not completion ordering.

C2_IMPLEMENT.evidence: Added a D3D11 event query, End->Flush->GetData(S_FALSE loop) completion fence before xrDestroySwapchain, with best-effort Flush fallback if query creation is unavailable, plus deterministic reset/transport verifier coverage.

red_review.missing_contract: 00453 used ID3D11DeviceContext::Flush only; Microsoft documents Flush as asynchronous, so there was no CPU-visible proof that GPU execution had completed before xrDestroySwapchain.

standards: Khronos OpenXR 1.1.63 xrDestroySwapchain requires all submitted graphics API commands referring to the swapchain to have completed execution before the call.
Microsoft ID3D11DeviceContext::Flush is asynchronous; D3D11_QUERY_EVENT with GetData reports when the GPU has finished prior commands.
